judgment: The checked methods conditionally support the current strategy as a checkpoint-driven default, not a settled product decision: keeping the adapter boundary internal preserves learning flexibility while provider contracts, real external maintenance, and support governance remain unproven. A supported public freeze becomes more credible only when authenticated multi-provider evidence, boundary stability, maintained external demand, and accountable compatibility and security operations converge. This judgment remains INCOMPLETE because every intensive pass had only one bound evidence source.
decision_boundary: Do not decide whether to freeze and publicly support the provider-plugin API. Describe plausible 18-month futures, cross-scenario implications, observable and discriminating indicators, collection ownership and cadence, and reassessment checkpoints for the later product decision.
next_action: Clarify whether the working strategy requires two provider adapters in total or two additional non-Codex adapters, establish a timestamped indicator ledger, and conduct the first formal evidence review by 2027-02-20 or earlier when a specified trigger fires.

key_judgments.statement: Provider-contract stability and ecosystem readiness form two useful but interacting uncertainties: plausible futures include convergence with or without maintained external demand, and continued churn with or without that demand.
key_judgments.confidence_basis: The scenario distinctions trace to the case observations, but they are structured possibilities rather than exhaustive or probabilistic forecasts and rely on one evidence source.

key_judgments.statement: Across materially different futures, robust work is to preserve measurable internal lifecycle seams, record authenticated critical-path and boundary-change evidence, define compatibility and security ownership, and distinguish maintained implementations from expressions of interest.
key_judgments.confidence_basis: The actions address gaps visible in every constructed future, but their costs and effectiveness have not been measured.

key_judgments.statement: The current internal-only strategy is conditionally supportable, but it weakens if authenticated integrations fit the boundary with little change, contributor interest becomes maintained code, and accountable compatibility and security operations become real; it strengthens if shared-contract churn or cross-provider divergence persists.
key_judgments.confidence_basis: The direction of change is explicit and evidence-bound, while the future provider behavior, demand conversion, and operational capacity remain unknown.

key_judgments.statement: A supported public freeze is not justified by interface decomposition alone because the case supplies no maintained external adapter, accountable compatibility policy, public support channel, remote settings read-back, or multi-provider live evidence.
key_judgments.confidence_basis: These absences are directly reported in the case, but the evidence base has not been independently corroborated.

key_judgments.statement: The most discriminating comparison would track shared-boundary changes, provider-local exceptions, maintenance effort, security findings, and contributor completion across authenticated internal integrations and a bounded external prototype using the same draft contract.
key_judgments.confidence_basis: The comparison directly addresses the principal dispute, but no such comparative evidence is currently bound and this report does not authorize running the prototype.

strongest_alternative: Expose a narrowly versioned, explicitly experimental contributor contract around the existing lifecycle seams without promising broad compatibility, while retaining provider-specific capabilities internally. This could reveal demand and abstraction failures earlier, but it may still create de facto support and security obligations that the project is not currently equipped to observe or contain.
assumptions: Additional authenticated provider integrations will expose decision-relevant shared-interface requirements rather than only provider-local authentication and launch differences.
The option value of keeping the boundary internal outweighs contributor delay, workaround proliferation, and later migration cost.
Documentation requests without maintained implementations are too weak a demand signal for a supported compatibility promise.
Compatibility policy, security triage, support intake, and settings read-back should be operational before supported publication.
Provider stability and ecosystem readiness remain the most decision-discriminating uncertainties despite possible wild cards or interactions.
unknowns: Whether Claude and Gemini can complete repeatable authenticated critical-path runs and what shared-boundary changes those runs would require.
Whether prospective contributors will implement and maintain adapters through provider or project changes.
The comparative maintenance, migration, support, and security-review costs of internal-only learning versus bounded external experimentation.
Future provider authentication and non-interactive contract stability, including the severity and frequency of breaking changes.
Available compatibility budget, support ownership, incident-response capacity, and the feasibility of remote settings read-back.
dissent: The challenge found that internal-only operation is not the only conceivable safe learning mode; an explicitly experimental contributor surface is materially different from freezing a supported API.
The strongest rebuttal is that even an experimental surface can create de facto expectations, expand attack surface, and consume support capacity before controls exist.

The provider threshold is ambiguous: the case says at least two provider adapters, while several method artifacts restate it as two non-Codex or two additional adapters; this could materially extend deferral.
It remains unresolved whether controlled external learning would reduce total interface risk faster than authenticated internal integrations.

checkpoint.trigger: Review formally on 2027-02-20, then at least every six months through the 18-month horizon; review earlier after a second relevant authenticated provider milestone, a maintained external adapter, a material provider-contract break, a provider automation removal, an adapter-related security incident, operational compatibility/security ownership, or adoption of a provider-neutral standard.
indicators: Repeatable authenticated critical-path results by provider, covering probe, launch, collection, cancellation, timeout/retry, model observation, and normalized errors.
Number and severity of shared-boundary changes and provider-local exceptions per integration and provider release, summarized monthly by the adapter-boundary maintainer.

External contributors progressing from documentation requests to runnable adapters maintained through at least one upstream or project change, reviewed monthly by the product or contributor-relations owner.

Current named owners and approved records for compatibility, versioning, deprecation, security intake, public support, incident response, and remote settings read-back, checked at release gates and quarterly.
Measured migration effort, support load, unresolved security exceptions, and unavailable or contradictory observations, recorded per event and reviewed at the checkpoint.
Provider-contract convergence or breaking changes across consecutive release cycles, reviewed per provider release and quarterly without treating a raw indicator count as proof.

limitations: All five intensive method passes had one bound evidence source, below their configured distinct-evidence minima; no method result claimed PASS.
All passes used the same Codex host and correlation group, so method diversity is not independent corroboration.
The selected methods are preview methods and have not undergone independent method-fidelity assessment.
The run used no network or additional provider calls and therefore did not verify current provider behavior, external demand, security readiness, or operational support capacity.
Scenario construction does not assign probabilities, make the futures exhaustive, or make the final product decision.
Deterministic validation can establish schema, evidence binding, ledger, status, digest, and correlation consistency; it cannot establish factual accuracy or decision quality.
